newsitem.title: USA: Derivatives users oppose latest accounting plan.
newsitem.headline: Derivatives users oppose latest accounting plan.

text.p: A proposal to change the way companies account for derivatives could result in inconsistent and misleading corporate reports, users of derivatives said at a conference here Wednesday.
The Financial Accounting Standards Board, the private group that sets accounting standards, in June released a draft proposal drastically revising derivatives accounting.
Officials attending an International Swaps and Derivatives Association conference here reiterated widely voiced criticisms of the FASB draft.
"Derivatives utilization will continue to change faster than anyone can write rules to deal with specific derivative use," said Peter Rugg, chief financial officer of Triton Energy Ltd.
Under the FASB proposal, all derivatives would be carried on a company's balance sheet, unlike the present treatment where some derivatives are listed off-balance-sheet.
The proposal would also limit the use of hedge accounting, forcing companies to sometimes report fluctuations in the value of derivatives holdings in their net income.

Requiring hedging contracts to be periodically revalued, or "marked to market," in some cases creates volatility in the current valuation of future transactions and therefore fails to report results according to management's intent, Rugg said.
Many common financing techniques using swaps face inconsistent accounting treatment under the FASB proposal, said David Morris, senior vice president at Chase Manhattan Bank.
For example, a bank may have an excess of loans paying interest at the prime rate. The bank could enter a basis swap to convert the loans to a LIBOR rate, Morris explained.

But under the FASB proposal, because the basis swap replaces one variable rate cash flow with another, it would not qualify as a hedge and would have to be marked to market, creating fluctuations in the bank's earnings, Morris said.
Other common transactions, such as use of forward swaps to hedge upcoming debt issues and rolling three-month futures hedges against variable rate income, would also be unsettled, Morris said.
